new.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Commissions for SCs and STs:
1. In 1990 the joint national commission for SCs and STs became a constitutional body under Article 338.
2. The 89th Amendment (2003) bifurcated it into the NCSC (Article 338) and the NCST (Article 338A).
3. The Commissions submit their reports to the Prime Minister, who lays them before Parliament.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the joint commission became constitutional in 1990, and the 89th Amendment (2003) split it into the NCSC under Article 338 and the NCST under new Article 338A. Statement 3 is wrong: the Commissions report to the President, and the reports are laid before Parliament. Hence A; B, C and D wrongly include statement 3 or drop statement 1.
new.tq: 89th = bifurcation; reports go to the President.

new.s: What does Article 338(9) of the Constitution provide?
o: It empowers the President to create State Commissions for Scheduled Castes
It requires the Union and every State to consult the National Commission for Scheduled Castes on all major policy matters affecting SCs
It gives the NCSC power to amend the Scheduled Caste list
It provides grants-in-aid to State SC Commissions
new.x: Article 338(9) obliges the Union and State Governments to consult the NCSC on major policy matters affecting SCs. It does not empower the President to create State commissions (a trap in CDCA); State SC Commissions are created by State law. The SC list is altered only by Parliament under Article 341, and grants-in-aid are under Article 275(1) for ST welfare.
new.tq: 338(9) = duty to consult NCSC; State SC Commissions come from State law.

new.s:

new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Mahad Satyagraha took place on 20 March 1927 and its centenary (2026-27) began on 20 March 2026. Statement 3 is wrong: the Manusmriti Dahan was on 25 December 1927, separate from the 1930 Kalaram Temple Entry at Nashik. Hence A; B, C and D wrongly include statement 3.
new.tq: Mahad 20 Mar 1927; Manusmriti Dahan 25 Dec 1927; Kalaram 1930.

new.s:
With reference to the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, consider the following statements:
1. It was originally enacted as the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955.
2. It was renamed the Protection of Civil Rights Act in 1976.
3. It extends to the whole of India except Jammu and Kashmir and the north-eastern States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Act was enacted under Article 17 as the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 and renamed in 1976. Statement 3 is wrong: the Act extends to the whole of India (APPSC 2019 and GS 2019 keys). Hence A; B, C and D wrongly include statement 3.
new.tq: PCR: 1955 Act, renamed 1976, extends to the whole of India.

new.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955:
1. Section 5 - Refusing admission to hospitals, dispensaries or educational institutions on the ground of untouchability
2. Section 12 - Court presumes the offence was committed on the ground of untouchability when committed against a member of a Scheduled Caste
3. Section 10A - Offences by companies
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
new.x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct (both MPPSC 2019 key facts): Section 5 covers refusal of admission to hospitals, dispensaries and educational institutions, and Section 12 raises a presumption when the victim is an SC member. Pair 3 is wrong: Section 10A provides for a collective fine; offences by companies fall under Section 14. Hence A.
new.tq: Sec 5 hospitals/schools; Sec 10A collective fine; Sec 12 presumption; Sec 14 companies.

new.s: Offences under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 are:
o: Non-cognizable and triable only by a Sessions Court
Cognizable only with prior sanction of the State Government
new.x: Under Section 15, offences under the PCR Act are cognizable and may be tried summarily; they are also non-compoundable (MPPSC 2019 accepted both descriptions). They are not non-cognizable or compoundable, are not reserved for Sessions Courts, and need no prior sanction.
new.tq: PCR offences: cognizable, summary trial, non-compoundable.

new.s:
With reference to the SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, consider the following statements:
1. Section 18 bars anticipatory bail for persons accused of offences under the Act.
2. Section 19 bars the benefit of probation for persons convicted under the Act.
3. The Act came into force on 30 January 1991.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Section 18 bars anticipatory bail (CrPC Sec. 438, now Sec. 482 BNSS) and Section 19 denies probation to convicts. Statement 3 is wrong: the Act, passed in 1989, came into force on 30 January 1990. Hence A; B, C and D include the wrong date.
new.tq: Sec 18 no anticipatory bail; Sec 19 no probation; in force 30 Jan 1990.
